search_space: Exhaustively swept all 512 Boolean prefixes consisting of one isolation value and eight common-arc values for the fixed orders m = 1, 2, ..., 8, in lexicographic order with False before True. The unique prefix with isolation true and all eight common-arc values true remains undecided for orders m > 8 and is not a counterexample.
witness_description: No finite witness is produced: checking common truncated arcs through any fixed order does not establish their existence for every positive order.
refutation_explanation: A counterexample would have to make P isolated in X ∩ Y while satisfying the premise for every positive integer m. The quote supplies neither a finite reduction of that unbounded premise nor bounded encodings of X, Y, Z, P, and their arc spaces, so an exhaustive finite search cannot certify such a counterexample.
